newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges all Americans to leave Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges all Americans to leave Zaire.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko will resign after nearly 32 years in power and has made his intentions known in a letter to President Bill Clinton, according to a report in Sunday editions of the New York Times.
"The decision for him to leave has been made," a senior American official is quoted as saying.

The major issue holding up the resignation appears to be whether rebel leader Laurent Kabila will seize undivided power or whether he will share it with other political forces, the newspaper reported.
Diplomats travelling with U.S. envoy to the United Nations, Bill Richardson, told the Times that Mobutu said in a letter to Clinton that he would quit.

"A bitter shouting match" took place between Mobutu and American parties on Tuesday after Richardson, the president's personal envoy to Zaire, delivered a letter from Clinton to Mobutu demanding face-to-face discussions with Kabila and urging him to "withdraw from the political scene immediately," the newspaper reported.
When Richardson returned the next day to meet with Mobutu, the Zairean president handed the American envoy a letter for Clinton saying he would resign, according to the Times.
Mobutu, 66, who suffers from prostate cancer, is expected to "say he is going away for medical treatment, meaning in effect that he would not return" to Zaire, U.S. diplomats told the newspaper.

In Washington on Saturday the U.S. State Department urged U.S. citizens in Zaire to leave and warned Americans not to travel to the war-torn nation, citing the "deteriorating security and political situation" and the "potential for unrest throughout the country."

In a statement released by State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, the government also said it was ordering the departure of all non-essential U.S. embassy personnel. The government earlier ordered dependents of U.S. embassy personnel to leave Zaire.

"The Department of State warns U.S. citizens to defer all travel to Zaire due to the uncertain political and security situation and the potential for unrest throughout the country ... The Department strongly urges U.S. citizens in Zaire to depart the country," said Burns.
